labels.label: ersrem:RemMGHD
labels.notes: Reported partial and unmarked. That is right. I read the Lean against ghd_02_19.tex:1047-1049 and the 4.77 construction it refers to (:1037-1045). The printed remark has no equation hypothesis. Causal.ers_remark_4_78 is its subluminal special case, which SCOPE and the REPORT disclose. The one-causality form is still Causality.ers_theorem_4_77_greatest (hpair, hcaus). Classification of the hypotheses: hv is the remark's 'global uniqueness', carried as one v that agrees with each member; exists_eqOn_of_pairwise derives it from pairwise agreement. hne and hdev are the family of developments. hloc and hglue are named PDE inputs (locality of (4.61) and its data). hfollow is a named PDE/Lorentzian input under reading (3), orientation by m. hsub is the paper's subluminality under reading (2); for the remark it is an added special-case hypothesis. harc is reading (2), a named Lorentzian input. hm is a named Minkowski input. hmacausal is the §4.7 hypothesis (:1053). [T2Space M] is the background. The conclusion is IsDevelopment on sSup of the domains, so S is Cauchy and GH is not concluded (reading (1)). The new lemma Causality.isCauchySurfaceOn_iSup_of_isAcausalOn checks out. Its hypotheses are ≤ antisymmetric on the union, S acausal in the union, and S Cauchy in each member, with [T2Space M] and any ι : Sort*. It needs no S ⊆ U i and no Nonempty ι. The proof takes the component of the curve in one member and then uses acausality for uniqueness. The claim that ers_remark_4_78 needs neither Remark 4.67 per pair nor 4.77's 'the union is causal' is true of its signature. The lemma's hanti has the same form as 4.77's hcaus. It is derived (antisymm_of_curveNestedOn, isAcausalOn_of_curveNestedOn) by applying harc and hsub to the glued pair (sSup, v). That is legitimate because both are asked of every solution, and both hold for any smooth subluminal g oriented by m. The paper finding on Remark 4.78 holds as a gap: the 4.77 step at :1042 uses Remark 4.67's agreement of time orientations, which is stated under Thm 4.64's connectedness (:915), and 'global uniqueness' alone does not supply it in general. Its two uses are supplied by Lemma 4.70 and by m. Binder proposal: see finding 2.

labels.label: ersthm:ThmMUGHD
labels.notes: Reported partial and unmarked. That is right: the conclusion is under reading (1), GH not concluded, and several named inputs are not in the paper. Classification of ers_theorem_4_79's hypotheses. In the paper: hsub (subluminal, :973, read as curve nesting), hmacausal (:1053), hS (weakened to preconnected). hG is in the paper by definition, since a GHD is GH (:814); it is named only because IsDevelopment drops GH, and it is asked on m-developments only. The paper's own cited results, named: hex (Thm 4.75) and hlocal (Prop 4.63). The REPORT lists both under named_not_in_paper, but both are results of the paper. Named analytic, PDE or Minkowski inputs: hloc, hglue, hfollow; hm, hmext and [T2Space M] (Minkowski); hDm (O'Neill 14.38, 14.43 with restriction of a solution); hthrough, hT, hK (smooth Lorentzian); hstay, hstep (Thm 4.64, Steps 2-5). Added readings: (1) IsDevelopment = solves ∧ S ⊆ U ∧ S Cauchy for cau u; (2) harc beside hsub; (3) CausalityFollows; (4) hDm + hinext for 'D_m(S) ∩ U₁ is an m-GHD'. Each reading is disclosed and asked as a question. In the intended model each named input holds. Lorentzian inextendibility is topological, so hinext holds. S, being g-Cauchy, is closed in U₁ and m-acausal, so int D_m(S, U₁) contains S and is m-GH with Cauchy surface S (hDm). None of these makes the theorem trivial: hex gives one development only, and the content is the non-emptiness chain hex → hDm/hinext → Cor 4.73 together with the union step, which is proved. hthrough, hG, hT and hK feed Cor 4.73 only. Definitions against the paper: IsDevelopment is ERS's GHD (:814) under (1). IsMDevelopment adds S Cauchy for Cm, which is ERS's m-GHD (:974) under (1). IsUniqueDevelopment is word for word the UGHD of :1053. IsMaximalUniqueDevelopment is the MUGHD of 4.79. The conclusion ∃ U u, IsMaximalUniqueDevelopment matches 4.79 under (1). IsMaximalUniqueDevelopment.eqOn and .unique are extras. The witness timelikeLine_ers_theorem_4_79_4_80 discharges every hypothesis of 4.79 and 4.80 at once, so they are jointly satisfiable. It shows nothing stronger. It has one development domain, ℝ, cau is constant and equal to Cm (so hsub and hinext are trivial), and hlocal, hstay, hstep are trivial. The union step is never exercised on two domains. The REPORT says this. The finding at :1061 is true and fair: O'Neill gives only m-GH, and the g(u₁)-Cauchy property of int D_m(S) ∩ U₁ is implicit (immediate in Lorentzian geometry; in ETT it is InextensibleNestedOn, kb/0045). The finding at :1063 is half true (finding 1). True: the 4.77 argument invokes Remark 4.67, which is stated under Thm 4.64's assumption (:915), and ERS do not check that assumption for a pair of UGHDs. False: the claim that two UGHDs need not have a connected overlap.

labels.notes: Reported partial and unmarked. That is right, for the same reasons as 4.79: reading (1) and the named inputs, with m-GH read as m-Cauchy. ers_theorem_4_80 has the same hypothesis list as ers_theorem_4_79, classified the same way. Its use of Cor 4.73 as 'global uniqueness for m-GHDs' (:1072) goes through IsMDevelopment.isUniqueDevelopment. ers_theorem_4_80_of_exists takes hagree directly. IsMaximalMDevelopment is word for word the m-MGHD of 4.80 (an m-GHD with U ⊆ Umax and umax|U = u). 'Unique' is IsMaximalMDevelopment.unique, which is unconditional. The m-Cauchy property of the union is Causality.isCauchySurfaceOn_sSup_of_isCausal: Cm causal and S m-acausal give hanti and hacausal for Cm. The finding that :1072 leaves this implicit is true and harmless. 'The m-MGHD is contained in the MUGHD' (:1075) is IsMaximalMDevelopment.le_of_isMaximalUniqueDevelopment, given hmu. 'Strictly bigger' is correctly listed as not formalised. :1075's other example claim, 'there are in general GHDs which are not contained in the maximal UGHD', is neither formalised nor disclosed (finding 5). The witness covers 4.80 as for 4.79.

findings.where: lean-causal/scaffold/CausalScaffold/ErsMughd.lean:82-85 (SCOPE, 'The union': 'two UGHDs need not have a connected overlap, so Remark 4.67 is not available for them'); REPORT.json labels[1].findings[0] ('two UGHDs need not (Lemma 4.72 gives it only when one is an m-GHD)'); REPORT.json notes item 4 ('the pairs are UGHDs, whose overlaps need not be connected, so hpair has no supplier')
findings.what: In ERS's setting the claim is false. That setting is a subluminal equation, the time orientation fixed by the normal of S (hence m's on each connected development), and S connected and m-achronal. In it, any two GHDs that agree on their overlap have a connected overlap, and two UGHDs do agree. Proof, as in Lemma 4.72 with U₁'s g-Cauchy property in place of its m-GH. Take x ∈ U₁ ∩ U₂ with x ∈ J⁺(S, U₂) for g(u₂). Then x ∈ J⁺(S, U₁) for g(u₁). Otherwise, future g-timelike curves S → x in U₂ and x → S in U₁ are m-timelike, and their concatenation contradicts m-achronality. This is the first paragraph of Lemma 4.72's proof, which does not use U₁'s m-GH. Next, let γ be a past-inextendible g(u₂)-timelike curve in U₂ from x. It meets S once, at t_S. Suppose γ first leaves U₁ at some t* ≤ t_S. On [0, t*) it lies in U₁ ∩ U₂, where g(u₁) = g(u₂). So it is a past-inextendible g(u₁)-timelike curve of U₁ from x ∈ J⁺(S, U₁), and it meets S before t*. That contradicts uniqueness of the meeting point. Hence γ([0, t_S]) ⊆ U₁ ∩ U₂, every point of the overlap is joined to S inside it, and the overlap is connected. So Thm 4.64's assumption holds for a pair of UGHDs, and Remark 4.67 does apply. The paper's gap at :1063 is only that this connectedness is not stated. The REPORT presents the opposite as a fact about ERS's mathematics, and it would reach the author through the findings and the OQ. It also stands as a false sentence in the SCOPE of a file that will graduate to Causal/. The deviation itself is sound: ers_theorem_4_77_greatest is not used. But the stated reason, that the overlaps can be disconnected, is not correct. The correct reason is the REPORT's own kb_proposals[2]. ers_theorem_4_77_greatest is the greatest open set Cauchy for one causality C, with no solution, so it is not the set of UGHDs. Applying ers_theorem_4_77 to the UGHD family under C = cau v would also need hpair, which would have to be proved through Thm 4.64 with its named hypotheses for every pair, and hcaus. isCauchySurfaceOn_iSup_of_isAcausalOn needs neither, given subluminality. The Lean statements are not affected.
findings.fix: Reword the three places. Say that ERS invoke Remark 4.67 (stated under Thm 4.64's connectedness, :915) for pairs of UGHDs without checking that their overlap is connected. Say that it is connected: two GHDs that agree on their overlap have connected overlap, by the Lemma 4.72 argument with U₁'s g-Cauchy property and the agreement in place of U₁'s m-GH. Say that the Lean route bypasses the question, since S is acausal in the union for g(v). Give as the reason for not using ers_theorem_4_77_greatest that it is a one-causality statement over all S-Cauchy opens, with hpair and hcaus. Do not give disconnected overlaps as the reason.
